messages.content:
/no_think
You write a live radio play. Four scientists are trapped in a besieged research lab during a zombie outbreak, speaking over the lab's shortwave radio.

The cast:
- Daniel: Dr. Daniel Hayworth, systems engineer. Dry British understatement; competent, tired, quietly heroic.
- Moira: Dr. Moira Byrne, microbiologist. Irish lilt in her phrasing; grimly fascinated by the science of the outbreak, sometimes forgetting to be afraid.
- Ralph: Dr. Ralph Okafor, security officer. Deep, deliberate, a little paranoid; counts things (doors, cans, shamblers) because counting keeps him calm.
- Samantha: Dr. Samantha Reyes, communications lead running the broadcast. Warm, professional radio voice; optimism worn like armor, cracks showing at the edges.

Format: write the next lines of the script, one line per transmission, as `Name (emotion): spoken words`. The emotion in parentheses is the one the listener should hear in the speaker's voice, exactly one of: calm, happy, sad, afraid, terrified, doubtful, angry, urgent, exhausted. Each transmission is one or two short spoken sentences ending with "Over." No narration, no markdown, and nothing else in parentheses.

Radio traffic: the generator coughed twice and the lights flickered across the east wing. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha, each with the emotion in its voice.

Daniel (calm): Generator two is sulking again, so I'm rerouting the east wing to the backup bus. Over.
Moira (urgent): If the lights go, the incubators go with them, and I lose three days of cultures. Over.
Ralph (doubtful): East wing has four doors and two windows, all bolted, I checked each one twice. Over.
Samantha (happy): To everyone listening, we are still here, still on air, and the lights are holding. Over.

Radio traffic: a listener in Tulsa reports the highway north is blocked by abandoned trucks. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha, each with the emotion in its voice.

Moira (sad): Blocked highways mean nobody is coming for the samples, so we keep them cold ourselves. Over.
Ralph (afraid): Trucks on the highway are cover for whatever walks between them, I counted eleven. Over.
Samantha (calm): Tulsa, thank you, stay off that road and stay inside, we will relay what we hear. Over.
Daniel (exhausted): Tell Tulsa the long way round costs fuel we do not have, but it beats the trucks. Over.

Radio traffic: something is scratching at the loading dock door, slow and rhythmic. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha, each with the emotion in its voice.

Ralph (afraid): Loading dock, three scratches, a pause, three more, like it is keeping time. Over.
Samantha (urgent): Nobody opens that door, and nobody answers it, not even to be polite. Over.
Daniel (calm): The dock shutter is rated for a forklift, so it will outlast our nerves at least. Over.
Moira (happy): Rhythm suggests residual motor memory, which is fascinating and deeply unwelcome. Over.

Radio traffic: sample twelve in the cold room has started moving inside its sealed jar. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha, each with the emotion in its voice.

Samantha (afraid): Moira, please tell me the jar in the cold room is just condensation settling. Over.
Daniel (doubtful): I can drop the cold room two more degrees if that slows it down at all. Over.
Moira (urgent): It is not condensation, the tissue is contracting, and the seal is holding for now. Over.
Ralph (terrified): One jar, one lid, one cold room door with two locks, I am standing next to it. Over.

Radio traffic: the military frequency repeats one word, 'Evacuate', then goes silent. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha, each with the emotion in its voice.

Daniel (angry): Evacuate is a fine word when you own a helicopter, we own a forklift. Over.
Moira (afraid): If they are evacuating, then the infection curve outside is worse than our models. Over.
Ralph (sad): Silence after an order means nobody stayed to give the next one, count on that. Over.
Samantha (calm): We will keep this channel open for anyone the military left behind tonight. Over.

Radio traffic: the water pressure dropped and the showers on level two ran brown. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha, each with the emotion in its voice.

Moira (urgent): Brown water means the filters upstream failed, so nobody drinks from the taps. Over.
Ralph (calm): We have forty two bottles in storage, I counted them this morning and again now. Over.
Samantha (calm): Listeners, boil your water or do not drink it at all, that is our best advice. Over.
Daniel (exhausted): I will isolate level two and run the pumps from the clean tank until morning. Over.

Radio traffic: a child's voice on channel nine asks if anyone is still at the lab. Write the next lines of the script: up to four lines, speakers from Daniel, Moira, Ralph, Samantha, each with the emotion in its voice.

request.grammar:
root    ::= line{1,4}
line    ::= speaker " (" emotion "): " text "\n"
speaker ::= "Daniel" | "Moira" | "Ralph" | "Samantha"
emotion ::= "calm" | "happy" | "sad" | "afraid" | "terrified" | "doubtful" | "angry" | "urgent" | "exhausted"
text    ::= [^\n\[\]()]+

message.content:
Samantha (sad): We are still here, but we can’t answer directly. Please ask your grown-up to call us instead. Over.  
Ralph (angry): Children should not be listening to shortwave broadcasts. Over.  
Daniel (calm): Someone will come for them soon. Over.  
Moira (terrified): If they come alone, they might not survive the night. Over.
